text: War is over! That is a real front page, printed on November seventh, nineteen eighteen. But the war was not over.
So who sent it? The bulletin was signed by Roy Howard, president of the United Press, in France.
Newspapers rushed it out so fast that in South Bend, they misspelled the word armistice.
By that afternoon, Secretary of State Robert Lansing denied it. The German envoys had not even met the Allies yet.
The source? Admiral Henry Wilson at Brest. He said it came from his office, on what appeared to be official information.
The real armistice was signed on November eleventh. Four days after the papers said: war is over.
